subject: Dedicated deployment: data-sealing attestation & evacuation plan

From: Matt Gomez <matt.gomez@novabank.com>

Subject: Request: proof of geo-sealing + decommission timeline for dedicated cluster

Ben – following up from our call this morning. For our internal audit we need a concise package proving that:  
1) Customer tenant data in a Dedicated deployment can be constrained to a single US region (no cross-region backups by default).
2) The sequence and timing of actions used to remove a tenant (evacuation, snapshot deletion, block device wipe, metadata purge) and how you evidence that each step completed.
3) Expected maximum timelines for full irrevocable deletion once we trigger a tenant purge (we need an upper bound for legal).

Can you provide a short attestation and sample artifacts (logs, playbook excerpt, and architecture diagram)? If possible we prefer something we can include in our SOC appendix.  

Thanks,
Matt

Subject: Re: Request: proof of geo-sealing + decommission timeline for dedicated cluster

Hi Matt, brief technical summary and attached artifacts below. I included a short evacuation checklist you can quote in your appendix.  

High level: Dedicated clusters are deployed to an AZ set within a single cloud region when a customer requests regional anchoring. By default we do not replicate customer persistent volumes to other regions. Backups/snapshots are disabled unless configured (and they are region-scoped).  

Evacuation & deletion flow (ordered steps):
1) Quiesce: stop new write traffic to tenant (API-level read-only) – immediate.
2) Drain KV caches and flush ephemeral KV shards to local disk – seconds-minutes depending on pressure.
3) Live snapshot removal: identify any stored snapshots for tenant in region and schedule synchronous delete (background GC).
4) Block device wipe: overwrite and zero the tenant block devices (cloud API wipe + internal overwrite if ephemeral) – typical upper bound: 24–72 hours for large volumes.
5) Metadata purge: remove tenant pointers, keys, and backups from config store and key vault – immediate once step 4 finishes.
6) Final verification: generate an erasure-log that contains timestamps and operation hashes. We keep a signed retention of the erasure-log for 90 days for customer dispute support, and then the logs are rotated per our retention policy.

Upper bound for irreversible deletion: we commit to 30 days maximum from purge request to final artifact completion for large tenants (worst-case blocks/replication). Small tenants commonly finish within 48 hours. The longer window accounts for in-flight snapshots and cloud vendor GC timing.

Attachments included: wipe-playbook-v2.pdf (playbook excerpt), region-seal-arch.png (diagram of anchoring), erasure-log-sample.csv (sanitized log).

Notes about evidence: the erasure-log contains operation ids, start/finish timestamps, and a SHA256 of the wiped device manifest. That should satisfy most auditors; if Novabank needs signed attestation we can produce a short notarized PDF.

Aditya – FYI on the retention of erasure logs and the 90-day holding period we discussed.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Director, Site Reliability, Redwood Inference
